meta.title: Raoul Pal - The Exponential Age - TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026
meta.thread_line: 4 threads · liquidity explains the crypto bear · intelligence doubling every 5 months drives a capex super cycle · blockchain as the agent-economy settlement layer · $100T crypto by 2035

snapshot: Raoul Pal calls this 'one of the most skewed risk-reward opportunities' in crypto in a while, though 'not a straightforward opportunity'.
Crypto's bear came from thin liquidity: **excess liquidity** (above GDP growth) is still below zero, so AI capex and crypto can't both rally at once.
He reads the year as a two-standard-deviation, mid-cycle correction and has been accumulating Bitcoin into sell-offs (June-July, Jan-Feb).
What he needs next: a weaker dollar, lower rates and oil, plus bank lending (Bessent, Warsh). He presumes an Iran resolution before the midterms.
Super-cycle thesis: intelligence per unit of energy doubles **every 5 months** (Reed's law), feeding the second-largest capex boom in history.
Blockchain is the settlement layer for AI agents; with possibly 25B agents next year, crypto's addressable market 'goes to infinity'.
Targets: total crypto market cap ~$10T in the next couple of years and ~$100T by about 2035, up from ~$2.5T.

themes.title: Why crypto bled while the Nasdaq didn't: no excess liquidity
themes.lead: Liquidity never ran a full cycle, and the excess left over went to AI, so crypto took the hit.
bullets: The **Everything Code** formula: GDP growth = population growth + productivity growth + debt growth. Aging populations cut the first two, and debt fills the gap.
Narrow US liquidity (Fed balance sheet, TGA, banks' Treasuries) leads Bitcoin by about 90 days and is still not great. 'I'm not kind of expecting fireworks yet'.
Excess liquidity above GDP growth is still below zero, so money rotates. As the AI trade slowed, Bitcoin rose: 'We don't have enough liquidity to drive two things'.
Shocks this year: a government shutdown last October, the '10/10' crypto crash, another shutdown in January, war with Iran, and a rising dollar, rates and oil.

Debt growth is now interest compounding ('paying your credit card with a credit card'). Bessent and Warsh want the banking system to lend more, and the debt refi cycle has stretched from 4 to 5.7 years.
Triggers he waits for: a weaker dollar, lower rates and oil. He presumes Trump pushes an Iran resolution before the midterms to get oil down.

quote.text: We don't have enough liquidity to drive two things.

themes.watch: Raoul concedes Bitcoin can decouple from liquidity, and that the market is in 'wait and see mode'.

names.name: Bitcoin (BTC)
names.blurb: Accumulated into the June-July and Jan-Feb sell-offs; ~1.5 SD oversold.

themes.title: Intelligence per unit of energy is the super-cycle engine
themes.lead: Raoul argues the real cycle is intelligence, and capex follows it for decades.
bullets: After Moore's law, he measures **intelligence per unit of energy**, now doubling every 5 months: the first observed case of Reed's law (Metcalfe squared). Intelligence 'jumped substrate' from carbon to silicon.
The chain: semiconductors lead intelligence, which leads capex, which leads productivity. The aim is to lift trend GDP so debt-to-GDP falls.
Early productivity: corporate profits per employee 'ripped' after a decade-long plateau as hyperscalers stopped hiring.
Amazon is the template. It began automating in 2017-18, stopped hiring 6 years ago, and **robots will outnumber its human workforce next year**.
Hyperscalers carry debt of only ~3.5% of market cap. This is the second-largest capex event ever, after the railroads' 35-year build.
Only ~30% of data centers due this year got built because of bottlenecks; the build runs into the 2030s, maybe the 2040s, including compute and energy from space.
Adoption is the fastest ever: ChatGPT reached 100M users in 1.5 months and is now ~1.1B. Solar costs are collapsing; power bottlenecks will just mean more spending on solar, gas and nuclear.

quote.text: We birthed apex intelligence. It's not humans any longer. It's AI.

names.name: Amazon (AMZN)
names.blurb: Working model of a fully automating economy; robots overtake staff next year.

themes.title: Blockchain as the settlement layer for an agent economy
themes.lead: Crypto overbuilt block space like 1990s fiber; Raoul says stablecoins, tokenization and agents are the demand arriving now.
bullets: Blockchain is the coordination layer where money, ownership, identity and contracts settle, including agents paying agents.
Stablecoins on trend reach ~$1T by 2030, which also absorbs the Treasuries Bessent needs to sell.

Real-world assets: he first wrote in 2013-14 that the whole financial system would move on-chain; equity, bond and derivative markets 'all of it is going to come on chain', which drives demand for layer ones.
Agents: OpenClaw only arrived in November, yet agents may already outnumber humans; most internet traffic is agentic, and agents use more tokens than humans do.
At Reed's-law speed, perhaps 25B agents next year; if 1% hold wallets, that's 250M new crypto users, a ~25% jump in wallets. The TAM 'has gone to infinity'.

quote.text: There are infinite economic actors coming. So, if there are infinite economic actors, then the TAM has gone to infinity.

themes.watch: Raoul says himself that the agent numbers are guesses: 'I don't even know the numbers and I can't guess them because I don't understand Reed's law either.'

themes.title: The $100 trillion path: adoption plus debasement
themes.lead: Raoul stacks three waves (financial system on-chain, agent adoption, ongoing currency debasement) on top of the biggest capex boom ever.
bullets: The crypto market cap's Metcalfe log-regression channel points to ~$10T in the next couple of years (if the bull market comes), then **~$100T by about 2035**, creating $97.5T of wealth.
Debasement continues because productivity takes time to cut debt-to-GDP; governments still have to pay the interest.
US-China: neither can let the other win, so capital spending is effectively unlimited, including money printing and changes to banking laws.
Japan is steepening its yield curve and weakening the yen to restart lending; the private sector, after two decades of deleveraging, is about to re-lever.
His playbook: accumulate into sell-offs and hold. Bitcoin hit ~1.5 SD oversold, not the full 2 SD.
themes.watch: The talk closes with a plug for his book *The Everything Code* (out November 3), which this framework comes from.

takeaways.title: Track excess liquidity (liquidity above GDP growth) as the gate for crypto, not headline liquidity alone.
Watch the dollar, rates and oil together; all three easing is Raoul's 'risk-on' trigger.
Scale into crypto on 1.5-2 standard-deviation sell-offs instead of chasing rallies.
Follow agent wallet adoption as the new-user metric for layer ones.
Treat power bottlenecks as a capex accelerant (solar, gas, nuclear), not a ceiling.

hot_takes.take: I think this is one of the most skewed risk-reward opportunities we've had in crypto for a while.
The pace of intelligence per unit of energy is doubling every 5 months.
the number of robots um will overtake people at Amazon's workforce by next year.
it tells you we get to 100 trillion dollars by about 2035
maybe it's 25 billion agents by next year.
We birthed apex intelligence. It's not humans any longer. It's AI.

glossary.def: Liquidity growth above GDP growth: the spare money that can flow to speculative assets.
Network value scaling with the number of possible subgroups, faster than Metcalfe's n²; Raoul's shorthand for 'Metcalfe squared'.
The cadence at which governments and corporates roll their debt; Raoul says it stretched from 4 to 5.7 years.
Currency losing purchasing power as money supply grows to service debt.
A base blockchain (e.g. Bitcoin, Ethereum) where transactions finally settle.
